clue.text: One in the car to overtake on changing green

parts.note: to overtake another vehicle is to pass it

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of green are rearranged, with on joining them to what comes before

explanation.surface: A driver puts their foot down to get past someone the moment the lights turn green.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme answer: Passenger is also a song by Iggy Pop.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone riding in a vehicle without driving it.

clue.text: Motorway stopped — hang about in snarl-up

indicators.note: a snarl-up is a tangle, so the letters are jumbled together
a word that is stopped is cut off before its end, so hang loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Traffic on a motorway grinds to a halt and drivers are told to hang about in the jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopped' reads as describing the motorway, but it acts on the word hang.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, the high-speed road network of Germany.

clue.text: This track would get us rising with a start

indicators.note: the clue works backwards: this answer with a put in front would give us the word for rising
joins the extra letter to the answer
the extra letter goes at the start of the answer

parts.note: an ascent is a rising or climb

explanation.surface: A trail that climbs steeply from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is told in reverse: put A at the start of the answer and you get ASCENT, a rising. So the answer is ASCENT with its A taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is the trail or track left by an animal, followed by hounds.

clue.text: Destination of 17 in song of this time and place

explanation.surface: A song about where the road leads, set in the here and now.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is ROAD; Talking Heads sang Road to Nowhere, so the destination of that road in song is nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking Heads' song title names the place the road leads to.

clue.text: Be creepy, strange, if not odd as this

definitions.text: Be creepy, strange, if not odd as this

indicators.note: strange letters are rearranged into a new order
letters that are not in odd positions are the even ones

parts.note: the even letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Something that is weird but not odd: a teasing riddle about being creepy.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of BE CREEPY are E, R, E, Y, which rearrange to the answer; the whole clue also describes it, as EERY is a spelling of eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Eery is a variant spelling of eerie, meaning strange and unsettling, so the clue as a whole describes it.

clue.text: See 23
Elaborate artwork might be this in the red

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drawn too much, overworked by the artist
second meaning: having spent more than is in a bank account

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as over-drawn; the second is the banking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An account in debt to the bank is overdrawn; a picture with too much drawing is also over-drawn.

clue.text: Bring kids up? Every year, a regular payment

parts.note: PA is short for per annum, Latin for each year
rent is paid at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Raising children costs a fixed sum every year.
explanation.walkthrough: PA stands for per annum.
explanation.definitionFit: To parent is a verb meaning to raise children as their mother or father.

clue.text: More silver-grey, finally white, hairs, unkempt

indicators.note: unkempt hair is messy, so these letters are disordered
finally points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: An ageing head of hair, going whiter and messier.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface picture of greying, untidy hair is the definition's own scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means ash-coloured, a pale grey, so this comparative is greyer still.

clue.text: Wading birds digesting fish with a plant

indicators.note: the birds have the fish and the extra letter inside them, as if swallowed

explanation.surface: Storks swallowing a fish along with a piece of greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like vegetation in the birds' meal, but it means an industrial site.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelworks is an industrial plant, a factory where steel is made.

clue.text: He's a peer, not entirely before time

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A nobleman who turns up not quite ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman, and a member of the peerage.

clue.text: One helps criminals — arsonist initially improved

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: An accomplice to criminals, with a fire-raiser's skills getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor or abetter is someone who assists or encourages another in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Wined and dined, get last couples out wandering around

indicators.note: each word loses its final pair of letters

explanation.surface: After a night of eating and drinking, the last pairs of guests are sent out to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: WINED, DINED and GET each drop their last two letters, leaving WIN, DIN and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A winding path meanders, twisting and turning rather than going straight.

clue.text: 'Whispering', best song on record?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a remark made quietly so others do not hear
second meaning: the A-side, the main track of a single

explanation.walkthrough: Read as A SIDE, the second meaning is the lead track of a vinyl single.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a quiet remark, and the A-side was the featured track on a single.

clue.text: It's cold in this place with restricted energy and disheartened refugees — these console

indicators.note: the energy is held in, restricted within the other letters
the heart of the word is removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: only its first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A cold camp short of power, and dispirited refugees given comfort by helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerers are people who lift others' spirits, which is what those who console do.

clue.text: Conceited 11 briefly became cruel, though not sad

parts.note: 11 is EARL, whose abbreviation is E
to get is to become, as in got cold

indicators.note: the word for sad is taken out of the longer word

explanation.surface: A self-important nobleman turned nasty, if not unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: E is a recognised abbreviation for Earl.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotistic describes someone vain and self-centred, full of their own importance.

clue.text: While listening, travelled Route 66 perhaps? (Is it 19 and 13?)

indicators.note: listening means we go by how the word is heard

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone motoring along the famous American highway, with a hint at a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a thematic aside: 19, 13 and this answer make The Long and Winding Road. Route 66 is the historic US highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Route 66 is an example of a highway, the famous one from Chicago to Los Angeles.

clue.text: Personal growth shown by that woman retaining extremely low frequency on record

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after
the pronoun holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: ELF is the standard abbreviation for extremely low frequency in radio

explanation.surface: A woman's self-improvement journey, recorded on a deep-voiced album.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-help is improving oneself by one's own efforts, a matter of personal development.

clue.text: Have yen, half the capital and $1000 in a single letter

indicators.note: only half of the city's name is kept, its first three letters

parts.note: a grand is a thousand, written as G

explanation.surface: Holding Japanese currency, part of a capital and a thousand dollars in one envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like Japanese money, but it is a craving. G for grand is slang for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a yen is to yearn or crave something, which is to long for it.

clue.text: Pleasant-sounding hard rock?

indicators.note: sounding means the answer is said the same way as the word for pleasant

explanation.surface: A query about heavy rock music that is easy on the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard rock looks like music, but it is geology; the G of this word is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a coarse metamorphic rock, banded and very hard.

clue.text: Dug out of bed? — shown to be false

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., removed from a bunk

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading treats DE- as 'off' and BUNK as a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth that is debunked has been exposed as a sham; jokingly, someone de-bunked has been hauled from their bunk.

clue.text: Song of scrambled circle by one in velodrome event

indicators.note: scrambled letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A song about riders circling in a velodrome race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song of' marks a theme entry: Bicycle Race is a Queen song.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is a banked cycle track, so its events are races between riders on bikes.

clue.text: Wee devil's ice cream vehicle song

parts.note: deuce is an old euphemism for the devil, as in what the deuce
a coupe is both a dessert dish of ice cream and a two-door car

explanation.surface: A little devil's song about an ice cream van.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Deuce Coupe is a Beach Boys song about a hot-rod car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beach Boys recorded this 1963 song, a celebration of a hot-rod Ford.

clue.text: He's in a state: "I twitch over Eastern philosophy"

indicators.note: over means turned the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: the letter I, taken as written from the quoted speech
a tic is an involuntary twitch
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A nervous person agitated, confessing to a twitch while studying meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' looks like agitation, but it means belonging to a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen is a member of a nation, someone belonging to a country.

clue.text: A part of this car if you can make series of scratches

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the following words, run together

parts.note: the answer runs through these words, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Vandalising a car by keying a line of scratches into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarify is to make shallow cuts or scratches, as on skin or a lawn.

clue.text: Turning part runs car beginning to go

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken away

explanation.surface: A car starting off, with runs and turning parts working.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating component of a machine, as in a helicopter or engine.

clue.text: See 22
This little fact is pretentious stuff

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that a small figure is just showy nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is informal shorthand for statistic, a small numerical fact.

clue.text: Wants special places like Motown

parts.note: Motown, short for Motor Town, is Detroit, a city built on carmaking

explanation.surface: Someone who craves exotic spots like Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wants' looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Wants in the sense of shortages or lacks are scarcities.

clue.text: See 23
TV plot with 17 in song

parts.note: a graph is a plot of data

explanation.surface: A television drama with a road-trip song.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is ROAD: Telegraph Road is a Dire Straits song.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire Straits' song Telegraph Road pairs this word with the road answer.
